patches.old:
“I sent these virgins to live with you because I saw that they were friendly toward you. So you have them as helpers, so that you can better keep his commandments. You cannot keep these commandments without them. I see that they are happy to be with you. I will tell them never to leave your house.”

2. “You only need to clean your house thoroughly. They are happy to live in a clean house. They are clean and chaste, they work hard, and the Lord favors them all. If they find your house pure, they will stay with you. But if even a little defilement gets in, they will leave at once. These virgins do not love defilement at all.”

3. I say to him, “Sir, I hope to please them so that they will always be happy to live in my house. You put me in this one’s care, and he has no complaint about me. They will have no complaint either.”

4. He said to that shepherd, “I know[a] that God’s servant wants to live. He will keep these commandments and give these virgins a clean home.[b]”

5. After saying this, he put me in that shepherd’s care again. He called the virgins and said, “I see that you are happy to live in this man’s house. I put him and his house in your care. Never leave his house.” The virgins were glad to hear this.

patches.reason: Restore the general impossibility expressed by Latin non potest enim fieri ut sine his virginibus haec mandata serventur. The passive haec mandata serventur concerns the keeping of these commandments generally, not only this recipient’s ability. This proposed correction preserves the categorical necessity without changing the existing bounded textual selections, footnotes, servant terminology, or paragraph divisions.
